concept.name: Liquid staking token
concept.definition: A liquid staking token (LST) is a transferable token issued by a liquid staking protocol (e.g. Lido's stETH) that represents a claim on staked assets plus accruing rewards, letting stakers stay liquid and use their stake in DeFi while validators do the work.
concept.intuition: It is a receipt for your staked ETH that trades like ETH itself — you earn staking yield while still being able to sell, lend or LP the receipt.
concept.mechanics: Users deposit ETH into the staking pool; the protocol stakes it across a set of professional node operators and mints stETH (or similar) to the depositor. The token's balance or exchange rate grows with staking rewards net of a protocol fee (Lido takes 10% of rewards), and it can be traded, used as collateral, or redeemed for the underlying (subject to withdrawal queues).
concept.formula: User APR ≈ protocol staking APR × (1 − protocol fee); e.g. 3.2% × (1 − 0.10) ≈ 2.9%.
concept.failure_modes: LSTs can trade below their underlying value (depeg) during market stress or withdrawal congestion, and leveraged looping of LST collateral unwinds violently when the peg slips; smart contract bugs, operator slashing and governance capture add layers beyond native staking risk.
concept.misconceptions: An LST is not pegged 1:1 by arbitrage the way a stablecoin is — secondary-market price floats and can deviate for months. 'Liquid' also does not mean instantly redeemable: native withdrawals queue, so liquidity depends on DEX depth.
concept.example: Deposit 10 ETH into Lido and receive ~10 stETH; a year later the position represents ~10.3 ETH of staking rewards, and throughout you could have supplied the stETH as Aave collateral to borrow stablecoins.

citations.source: Lido docs - What is Lido / Liquid staking
